newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco area home sales, prices level off.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco area home sales, prices level off.

text.p: San Francisco Bay area home sales dropped slightly in June from May's pace, but were expected to level off in the coming months, according to a report on Thursday.

A total of 5,924 resale houses were sold in the nine county San Francisco Bay area in June, down 3.6 percent from 6,145 for May and up 8.1 percent from June a year ago, according to a report by DataQuick Information Systems.
"We're expecting sales counts to level off at the current fast pace," Mike Ela, DataQuick's president, said in a statement.
The median price for a house in the Bay area was $257,000 last month, up 4.0 percent from $247,000 in June 1996.
The median had jumped from $239,000 in March to $260,000 in April, an uncommonly steep month-to-month surge. The median held firm at $258,000 for May, DataQuick said.

DataQuick monitors real estate purchasing and financing nationwide. Its San Francisco area report includes the counties of Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Solano and Sonoma.
